dedupe_keys.name: green infrastructure case studies municipal policies for managing stormwater with green infrastructure us epa 12 local governments 2010

description: This US Environmental Protection Agency report compares how twelve local governments developed and implemented stormwater policies that support green infrastructure. The 76-page report (EPA-841-F-10-004, August 2010) read on 2026-09-28 covers Alachua County, Chicago, Emeryville, Lenexa, Olympia, Philadelphia, Portland, San Jose, Santa Monica, Seattle, Stafford County and Wilsonville. It describes the common drivers, such as combined sewer overflow and municipal separate storm sewer permit requirements, asset management, flood control and wider sustainability goals; a menu of local policies, from stormwater regulations, code revisions and pilot projects to capital and transport projects, outreach, stormwater fees, fee discounts and other incentives; and the barriers, lessons and realities of each policy, grouped as first, second and third step policies, with a short profile of each place. Coverage is the United States. Access is free on the EPA NEPIS service; the report states no licence. Caveats: it is from 2010 and qualitative, without cost or performance data. It supports stormwater adaptation planning by showing which policies cities combined to scale up green infrastructure. No related EPA green infrastructure record is catalogued.
